about: Inputs of the season simulator (backend/engine/vaari_engine/sim). Every input is labelled: 'real range' (taken from a cited source or real data) or 'assumed' (our choice, stated, and swept where it could change the answer). Farmers, fields, machines, breakdowns and rain are SIMULATED; village positions (OpenStreetMap) and harvest timing (NASA FIRMS) are real. Each input is sourced, or labelled assumed and swept. The headline's 2 days for farmers without a date is an assumption the team chose and the page says so.

harvestReadyDay.label: real range
harvestReadyDay.rule: drawn from each village's harvest curve in data/harvest_curves.json, inside the season window
harvestReadyDay.source: NASA FIRMS VIIRS standard-processing detections from S-NPP and NOAA-20, 2024 and 2025, over the Sangrur box, shifted 3 days earlier than the fire (the shift is assumed; see data/README.md). NOAA-21 is left out: FIRMS has it only as near-real-time data

seasonWindow.label: assumed
seasonWindow.why: 11 October to 25 November (day 0 = 1 October) holds about 90% of the district harvest curve; earlier and later fields are left out

district.label: real range
district.rule: the real outline of Sangrur and Malerkotla districts (Malerkotla was formed from Sangrur in 2021), and every village inside it within the demo box
district.source: OpenStreetMap administrative boundaries and village points (data/boundaries.json, data/villages.json)

machineCentres.label: assumed
machineCentres.rule: the first at the village with the most fire detections, the rest spread over the district by farthest-point sampling and balancing rounds; every village is served by its nearest centre
machineCentres.why: no public list of the district's rental centres; 25 centres of about 4 machines each puts about 100 Super Seeders to rent across the district

machines.label: assumed
machines.why: machines per centre on average; each centre's fleet is in proportion to the villages it serves (at least one), so every machine carries the same acres

acresPerMachine.label: assumed
acresPerMachine.why: acres booked with the CHC per machine in a season. The value is the middle of what CEEW reports real Super Seeders cover: about 100 acres is the optimum (break-even near 105), one entrepreneur covers about 120, the Noorpur Bet cooperative about 175. Farmers are drawn until the season holds this many acres per machine; swept below
acresPerMachine.source: CEEW, Custom Hiring Centres for Better Crop Residue Management: Insights from Punjab (2025)

fieldAcres.label: assumed
fieldAcres.why: acres per booking, mean 6. CEEW: a median government CHC serves about 300 acres for 50 farmers (6 each), a median private CHC 75 acres for 10, Noorpur Bet 750 for 150. The spread (many small farmers, a few large) is our choice; no per-field data
fieldAcres.source: CEEW, Custom Hiring Centres for Better Crop Residue Management: Insights from Punjab (2025)

waitingLimitDays.label: assumed
waitingLimitDays.why: days a farmer waits after harvest before burning; swept below

daysSoonerWithoutDate.label: assumed
daysSoonerWithoutDate.why: how many days sooner a farmer with no date gives up and burns than one holding a promised date. CEEW and Shyamsundar et al. (Science, 2019) find uncertainty over getting a machine is a main reason farmers burn, but no source measures it in days. The headline assumes 2 days (the team's choice, labelled on the page); the sweep below shows 0 to 3
daysSoonerWithoutDate.source: CEEW, Why paddy stubble burning continues in Punjab (2024); Shyamsundar et al., Science 365 (2019)

afterLastWaitingDay.label: assumed
afterLastWaitingDay.rule: a farmer not sown by their last waiting day burns the stubble, leaves the queue, and sows with an ordinary drill the next day; the CHC loses that booking
afterLastWaitingDay.why: CEEW: uncertainty over when the machine comes is a main reason farmers burn

requestLeadDays.label: assumed
requestLeadDays.why: farmers call 0 to 3 days before their paddy is harvested

phoneQueueRentals.label: assumed
phoneQueueRentals.rule: the phone queue is a rental desk: each rental is a trip from the CHC to the farmer and back, and the next caller's rental starts from the CHC
phoneQueueRentals.why: CEEW: most CHCs rent first come, first served, by phone or in person; only 39% of government CHCs offer a tractor-and-driver package (the rest rent the machine alone, by the hour or day); sending the machine straight from one farmer to the next is a best practice some CHCs adopted to avoid repeated returns to the CHC
phoneQueueRentals.source: CEEW, Custom Hiring Centres for Better Crop Residue Management: Insights from Punjab (2025)

phoneQueueLateReturnChance.label: assumed
phoneQueueLateReturnChance.why: the chance that a phone-queue rental comes back late, so the machine is gone for the rest of that day. CEEW: 45% of renting CHCs report delayed returns, 62% of those renting the machine without a driver (38% with one), but no source gives a rate per rental. The base season uses 0; swept below. Vaari and nearest village next are driver-run, so this applies to the phone queue only
phoneQueueLateReturnChance.source: CEEW, Custom Hiring Centres for Better Crop Residue Management: Insights from Punjab (2025)

nearestVillageRule.label: assumed
nearestVillageRule.rule: nearest village next is a driver-run service: after each field the driver goes straight on to the nearest booked field that is ready
nearestVillageRule.why: the strongest simple routing rule an operator could follow without a planner

machineAcresPerDay.label: real range
machineAcresPerDay.source: CEEW operator interviews: about 5.3 acres in an 8-hour day (the low end). Each machine's true speed is drawn from this range and Vaari learns it from the day's work
machineAcresPerDay.alsoSource: The Tribune, Jalandhar (2019), reporting an agriculture department camp: a Super Seeder sows 10 to 12 acres a day (the high end)

setupMinutesPerField.label: assumed
setupMinutesPerField.why: turning in and lowering the implement

roadSpeedKmh.label: assumed
roadSpeedKmh.why: tractor with implement on village roads

rainChancePerDay.label: assumed
rainChancePerDay.why: no sowing on a rain day; forecast the evening before

optimumLastDay.source: PAU Package of Practices, Rabi 2025-26: first fortnight of November is the optimum

rentRupeesPerAcre.source: CEEW CHC publication: full Super Seeder package

strawTonnesPerAcre.unit: tonnes of paddy straw per acre
strawTonnesPerAcre.source: Punjab Pollution Control Board, report to the NGT in OA 632 of 2023: 6.5 tonnes per hectare for non-basmati paddy (6.5 / 2.471 acres per hectare)

burnCombustionFactor.unit: share of the straw that combusts when a field is burned
burnCombustionFactor.source: IPCC 2006 Guidelines, Vol. 4, Table 2.6 default, as used for Punjab by Bhadauriya, Chaudhary, Mamatha and Ray, ISPRS Archives XLIII-B3 (2020), p. 1423

pm25GramsPerKgStrawBurned.unit: grams of PM2.5 per kg of rice straw burned
pm25GramsPerKgStrawBurned.source: Gadde et al., Environmental Pollution 157 (2009), rice straw open burning, as used for Punjab by Bhadauriya, Chaudhary, Mamatha and Ray, ISPRS Archives XLIII-B3 (2020), p. 1423

base.about: the whole district: every centre's farmers and machines, the district's weather

capacityShortfall.about: the same district seasons with half the machines (each centre keeps half its fleet, rounded half up, at least one) and the same farmers: too few machines for the acres booked, so no way of working can sow everyone before they give up

sweeps.about: the base seasons with more or fewer farmers: acres booked per machine, across and just past the range CEEW reports
the base seasons with every farmer waiting exactly this many days
the base seasons with farmers who have no promised date giving up this many days sooner
the base seasons with this share of phone-queue rentals coming back late (the machine is gone for the rest of that day)

planner.about: Vaari plans each evening with the search planner (seeded, reproducible)

sweepScope.about: each sweep replays the district's first centre (the fire hotspot) alone, 50 seasons per value, to keep a full run on a laptop

seasons.about: a full run plays 50 seasons of the whole district
